chapter: Arranging craft, ownership and the business
title: A woman arranger's teachers and atonality in school
summary: They discuss an arranger who studied with Rayburn Wright, Bob Brookmeyer and Gil Evans and was laughed at for writing in a key.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah, speaking of when I asked a question about something new I think she found a way to add a new thing to the big band repertoire it seems like.

Yeah. She studied with Rayburn Wright, who I also studied with, but I think she really found her groove when she studied with Bobby Brookmeyer and Gil Evans, when she started listening to them and studying with them. That really helped her a lot. And I think it reinforced her whole body of work. She probably had that diatonic sense she has today back then but I think they really molded it for her.

Yeah she told me this, I won’t get off on a tangent here, this will only take a second but it was a very interesting thing when she went to college and she wrote a piano — a piece for two pianos, that the professors laughed at it quietly because it was in a key.
And everybody was into atonality at the time.
